messages.subject: break up y-axis for boxplots
parts:
Hi @all

I was just wondering if it is somehow possible to break up the y axis
for boxplots? I have several outliers and I don't want to remove them
for the boxplots. Any ideas because I couldn't find any solution to
that problem so far. Thanks, Martin.

Here is the code:
dodge <- position_dodge(width = .9)

read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/nutrients_new_sw.csv") ->
nutrients_sw

melt_nutrients_sw <- melt(nutrients_sw, id=c("ID", "round", "Season",
"catchment"),na.rm=TRUE)

melt_nutrients_sw$catchment <- factor(melt_nutrients_sw$catchment)

p <- ggplot(melt_nutrients_sw, aes(x = catchment, y = value, color =
Season))
p + geom_boxplot(position=dodge) + facet_grid(variable~ ., scales =
"free") + opts(legend.background=theme_rect(colour=NA)) +
scale_x_discrete()

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: break up y-axis for boxplots
parts:
Hi Martin:

I'd suggest using facet_grid(variable ~ ., ...) instead. The problem with the
current display is that the boxplots are squashed and the effect of outliers
is not easy to see.

p + geom_boxplot(position=dodge) +
      facet_grid(. ~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
      opts(legend.background=theme_rect(colour= NA)) +
      scale_x_discrete()

Alas, this gives a common scale for all the responses, but the outliers are
obvious :)  I don't quite understand why the vertical scale is the same for
all panels, though....  OTOH, the range isn't overly extreme and it provides
a way to compare the different responses in a fairly clean way.

To compensate for the common y scale, you could try a couple of
different vertical scales - e.g., square root or log_2. Add either
scale_y_log2()  or   scale_y_sqrt()     to the end of the call above. The
purpose is to spread out, to the extent possible, the concentration of
values near zero. Both transformations have the effect of shrinking large
values and spreading out very small values. I prefer the log scale, but
opinions may differ. Just a thought...

HTH,
Dennis

parts:
Hi Dennis

I tried your suggestions but I wonder if there is a better solution
than just transferring the y-axis by square root or log. Is it somehow
possible to separate the data into two sets (eg. normal values and
outliers) and than plot them together but with different scales?

Thanks, Martin
